_note: The claim catalogue (DR 22; W-117a, D-699): how a deduction or exemption is claimed. One entry for a rule: a rule is named, as an entry's rule or in its covers, once. Texts type no figure — a figure comes from a {{RuleId.field}} placeholder, a section number from basis. Each year's pack keeps the entries whose rule it holds, covering only the rules it holds.

entries._sources: channel, ifMissingFromForm16: Income-tax Act, 2025, Gazette CG-DL-E-22082025-265620 — s.11(1) (p.36) and Sch. III preamble (p.504) and Table Sl. 11 (p.506): the exemption's conditions (a) – (d) are the allowance's purpose, the prescribed extent, a home not owned, and rent actually paid — none is proof given to an employer; s.392(5)(b) (p.397) puts the duty to obtain evidence of prescribed claims on the employer. So the return takes the claim (owner's ruling, session 97, option (a)). s.392(4)(a)'s "at his option" (p.397) covers five other particulars and is not this entry's basis (erratum on DR 22 C2). provision1961: s.10(13A) and its Explanation, thc.nic.in consolidated Income-tax Act, 1961 (current to Act 7 of 2019) PDF p.77 — the same conditions, none about proof given to an employer (W-117b C3a; sources/2026-11-14-claim-channel.md C16). steps[2]: SAL-HOUSE-RENT-LANDLORD-PAN (r.205(2) Table Sl. 1; sources/2026-10-09-landlord-pan.md). steps.instruction: Keep a rent receipt for every month you pay rent.
steps.produces: A receipt for each month's rent.

steps.instruction: If your rent for the year is more than {{SAL-HOUSE-RENT-LANDLORD-PAN.exceeds}}, get your landlord's name, address and PAN.
Give the receipts and those details to your employer on the declaration form they give you.
If you missed your employer's cut-off, claim it in your return instead.

askWhom.askFor: Their name, address and PAN, where your rent is above that figure.
The declaration form for your rent, and the last day they take proofs.

evidence.name: Rent receipts
evidence.closedBy: A receipt for each month you paid rent.

evidence.name: Your landlord's particulars
evidence.closedBy: Their name, address and PAN, where your rent is above that figure.

mistakes: Leaving dearness allowance out of the salary the limits are measured on.
Claiming for the whole year when you lived there for part of it.
Claiming for a home you own and live in.

entries.appliesTo: A donation to a charitable institution or fund that has to report it to the tax department. Other donations are not covered here.

steps.instruction: Ask the institution whether it reports your donation to the tax department.
Get its certificate of the donation.
steps.produces: The institution's certificate of your donation.

steps.instruction: Check that the donation appears in your annual information statement before you file.

askWhom.askFor: Its certificate of your donation, and whether it has reported the donation to the tax department.

evidence.name: The institution's certificate
evidence.closedBy: The certificate it issues once it has reported the donation.

mistakes: Claiming a donation the institution has not reported.
Claiming a cash donation above the limit.

steps.instruction: Start from the provident fund your employer already takes from your salary: it counts towards this deduction.
Add what you paid in the year: life insurance premiums, your children's tuition fees, the principal repaid on your home loan and the listed savings schemes.
steps.produces: A receipt or statement for each payment.

steps.instruction: Give the proofs to your employer on the declaration form they give you.
Claim in your return whatever your employer did not count.

askWhom.askFor: The declaration form for your investments, and the last day they take proofs.
A statement of what you paid in the tax year.

evidence.name: Payment receipts and statements
evidence.closedBy: A receipt or statement for each payment, dated in the tax year.

Counting home-loan interest here: only the principal repaid counts.
Counting development fees or donations to a school as tuition fees.

Pay the rest into your own pension scheme account before the tax year ends.
steps.produces: Your pension scheme account statement for the year.

steps.instruction: Give the statement to your employer on the declaration form they give you.
If you missed your employer's cut-off, claim it in your return instead.

Get the insurer's certificate of each premium, showing the period it covers.
steps.produces: The insurer's certificate of the premium.

steps.instruction: Note the age of each person insured, your parents included: a senior citizen has a higher limit.
Where you paid a premium for several years at once, count only this year's share.
Give the certificates to your employer on the declaration form they give you.
If you missed your employer's cut-off, claim it in your return instead.

steps.instruction: Get your lender's certificate of the interest payable for the year, showing any later loan taken to repay the first.

Check your limit: up to {{HP-OWN-RESIDENCE-INTEREST-CAP.conditionsMet}} where the loan bought or built the home, the work was completed within the time the law allows and you hold the lender's certificate; up to {{HP-OWN-RESIDENCE-INTEREST-CAP.anyOtherCase}} otherwise; never more than {{HP-OWN-RESIDENCE-INTEREST-CAP.aggregate}} for all your homes together.
If you want less tax deducted from your salary, give your employer the loss from your home on the declaration form they give you.
Claim it in your return either way.

askWhom.askFor: A certificate of the interest payable for the year, including on any loan taken to repay the first.
The declaration form for a loss from your home, and the last day they take it.

evidence.name: Lender's certificate of interest
evidence.closedBy: The certificate for the year, from the person the interest is payable to.

mistakes: Counting principal repaid as interest: the principal belongs with your investments.
Using the higher limit when the home was not completed in time after the loan was taken.

entries.appliesTo: Travel assistance your employer actually paid you for a journey in India. With no assistance from your employer there is nothing to claim.

steps.instruction: Check that your employer pays you travel assistance: without it there is nothing to claim.
Travel in India and keep the tickets for each journey.
steps.produces: A ticket for each journey and each person travelling.

steps.instruction: Check how many journeys you have already used in the current block of calendar years.
Claim through your employer's process, with the tickets.
If your employer paid the assistance but taxed it, claim it in your return.

askWhom.askFor: Their process for claiming travel assistance, and the last day they take tickets.

evidence.name: Travel tickets
evidence.closedBy: A ticket for each journey and each person travelling.

mistakes: Claiming without having travelled.
Treating the block of years as tax years: it runs in calendar years.
